lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: handwashing a small item

objective: Learners handwash one small stained item, pretreating the stain with a small amount of detergent rubbed directly into the fabric before soaking, washing, and rinsing, building on the basic handwashing technique from third grade by adding a targeted pretreatment step for a real stain.
scenario: A trusted adult identifies one real small item with a visible stain, such as a bandana, a sports sock, or a cloth napkin. The learner examines the stain, pretreats it, then completes the full wash-and-rinse loop with the adult present, checking at the end whether the stain lightened or came out.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult stays present for the entire pretreat-wash-rinse sequence.
Use only cool or lukewarm water; never water hot enough to be uncomfortable to the touch.
Check with the adult before using any stain-treatment product beyond plain detergent; some products require adult-only handling.

simulationAlternative.description: If no stained item is available, the learner instead studies a printed photo or description of a stained item and writes the four-step plan they would follow (identify the stain, pretreat, wash, rinse and check), including one reason pretreating before washing works better than washing first.

materials: a place to hang the item to dry

tasks.directions: Look closely at the stain with your adult before starting.

prompts.text: Describe the stain: what color is it, roughly how large, and where on the item is it located?

tasks.directions: With your adult present, rub a small amount of detergent directly into the stained area and let it sit for two minutes before wetting the whole item.

prompts.text: I rubbed detergent directly onto the stain, not just onto the whole item evenly.
I let the pretreated stain sit for about two minutes before wetting the item.
I then washed and rinsed the whole item using the four-step routine from third grade.

tasks.directions: After rinsing, check the stained area closely before hanging the item to dry.

prompts.text: Compared to before pretreating, is the stain gone, lighter, or unchanged?
If the stain is still visible, what would you or your adult try next?

tasks.directions: Compare this task to plain handwashing without pretreating.

prompts.text: Explain why pretreating a stain before washing the whole item works better than washing the whole item first and hoping the stain comes out.

remediation: If a learner rubs detergent evenly across the whole item instead of targeting the stain, reteach with a marked practice cloth: mark a small circle with washable marker, have the learner pretreat only inside the circle, and check that the surrounding fabric stayed untouched.
extension: Have the learner pretreat and wash a second stained item using a different pretreatment wait time (for example five minutes instead of two) and compare which wait time got a better result.
